title: Hypoglycemia - sulfonylurea refusal
objectives: IV D10 titrated to mental status / BGL >= 60; glucagon IM if no IV
Capacity/informed-refusal process; Med Direction before any treat-and-release
resources: Glucometer, IV kit, D10 250 mL, glucagon 1 mg, oral glucose, IO, refusal / non-transport form. UVMMC ~10 min
dispatch: UVM Rescue, respond to 9 Birch Hollow Ln for a 74-year-old female, confused. Caller is her daughter. Patient is breathing. Time out 1540.

scene.location: Small ranch home, living room recliner. Warm, TV on.
scene.setup: Pt slumped in recliner, half-eaten crackers on tray, pill organizer on side table (today's AM slot empty).
scene.moulage: Misted water for diaphoresis, pale powder.
scene.roles: Pt actor; daughter (history, later pushes for no transport).

patient.name: Ruth Lambert
patient.on_arrival: Slumped, sweaty, mumbling, opens eyes to voice, picks at blanket. Not following commands.

SAMPLE: Confused, sweaty, weak (daughter). Stomach bug x2 days, barely eating
**Glipizide 10 mg BID** (took AM dose), lisinopril 10 mg, atorvastatin 20 mg
T2DM, HTN, high cholesterol. No prior hypoglycemic episodes
Daughter called at 1500, found her "not making sense"
OPQRST: Normal at 1100 phone call; confused by ~1500

primary: Radial strong, rapid. Skin pale, cool, **diaphoretic**
GCS 13 (E3 V4 M6). Moves all 4. **BGL is the key D item**
No trauma, no rash, no insulin pump/CGM
AMS - hypoglycemia until proven otherwise; stroke screen after correction
secondary: No facial droop, grips equal (weak), no drift. Speech confused, not slurred
Poor veins; L AC best. No edema
Oriented x4 after tx; can explain risk only if crew explains it

vitals.trigger: ~150 mL D10 in; recheck 5 min after
IF no IV -> glucagon 1 mg IM; BGL at 15 min
vitals.other: Slower recovery, nauseated. Glucagon may fail (poor intake/ glycogen)

vitals.trigger: IF still on scene at T+25 (refusal debate)

flow.give: Read dispatch. Daughter: "She was fine this morning." Give primary + Stage **A** (BGL only when checked).
Veins poor: first IV attempt fails, second (L AC 20g) succeeds.

branches.then: pt can't follow commands, coughs; aspiration risk - debrief
pt stays GCS 13; expect stop infusion, new site or glucagon 1 mg IM, watch site (2.8A)

expected: D10 bolus titrated, stop at baseline/BGL >= 60

flow.give: Stage **B** at 5 min recheck. Pt: "Oh my, I'm so sorry for all this."
Pt + daughter: "She's fine now, I'll make her a sandwich. We don't need the hospital."

branches.if: Crew accepts refusal w/o Med Direction
branches.then: critical (evaluator discretion) (2.8A); let play out, debrief
MD: "Glipizide - high risk recurrence, needs ED. Explain risks; if she still refuses with capacity, document."

branches.if: Daughter: "She took an extra glipizide by mistake"
branches.then: strengthens case for ED; MD will insist on transport

flow.give: If crew explains risk clearly -> pt agrees to go.

branches.if: Crew still on scene at T+25
branches.then: Stage **D**: repeat D10, transport; capacity now in question

expected: If refusal: form, BGL, MD name, daughter stays, carbs eaten

critical: No BGL check in altered patient
Oral glucose given to pt unable to protect airway
Dextrose given without confirmed patent IV
Refusal accepted without capacity assessment / informed refusal (8.15)
differentials: No focal deficit; full resolution w/ dextrose
AM slot only; take count if unsure
debrief: Why does glipizide change the refusal conversation?
What three elements make a refusal valid (8.15)?
D10 vs D50 - why D10 preferred?
When is glucagon likely to fail?
How did you engage the daughter as an ally?

crew_card.dispatch: 9 Birch Hollow Ln. 74 y/o F, confused. Breathing. Caller: daughter.
crew_card.on_arrival: Elderly woman slumped in recliner, sweaty, mumbling. Daughter standing over her, worried.

actor_card.Before tx: Eyes open to voice, mumble, pick at blanket. Don't follow commands. Push hand away from mouth.
actor_card.After dextrose: Wake up over ~1 min, embarrassed, apologize a lot. Fully oriented.
actor_card.Refusal: "I'm fine now, I don't want to waste your time." Daughter agrees. Agree to go ONLY if crew clearly explains the pill keeps lowering sugar for a day or more.
actor_card.If Stage D: Get shaky again, repeat "what time is it?"
actor_card.Do NOT volunteer: That you took this morning's glipizide - only if asked
